source.label: Original standalone fiction: the station piano
source.text:
This is original standalone fiction for a social edition. Mara is a fictional station cleaner. The story is not part of an established fictional universe.

At six each morning, Mara dusted the station piano. Its lowest key stayed down. She cleaned around it because the repair notice had been there longer than she had.

On a wet Thursday, she found a folded score beneath the lid. Every bar held the same small chord. Above it, someone had written: Play this when you can stay until it stops.

Mara had seven minutes before the next platform needed cleaning. She played the chord once. A man beside the departures board lowered his phone. A child stopped dragging her suitcase.

The broken key held one note after Mara lifted her hands. She waited with the others. When the note finally faded, her seven minutes were gone. She folded the score and left it where she had found it.

The next morning, the score was still there. Beneath the instruction, another hand had added: I stayed.

Adapt the complete story into six carousel panels, a newsletter with a short writing exercise, and a narrated video script. Preserve the small physical details and the restrained ending. Artwork, narration and music remain production tasks. Use an original or properly licensed score if audio is made.

artifacts.title: I stayed: six panels
artifacts.content:
Panel 1
At six each morning, Mara dusted the station piano.
Its lowest key stayed down.

Panel 2
The repair notice had been there longer than she had.
On a wet Thursday, she found a folded score beneath the lid.

Panel 3
Every bar held the same small chord.
Above it: Play this when you can stay until it stops.

Panel 4
Mara had seven minutes.
She played once.
A man lowered his phone. A child stopped dragging her suitcase.

Panel 5
The broken key held one note after Mara lifted her hands.
She waited.
When it faded, her seven minutes were gone.

Panel 6
The next morning, someone had added two words beneath the instruction:
I stayed.

Caption
A small story for anyone who has waited for a sound to finish.
What would you leave under the piano lid?

Production direction
Keep the station ordinary: damp coats, tired wood, a handwritten repair notice. Let the final panel leave space around the two words. This is finished slide copy; artwork is still required.

artifacts.title: Two words beneath the score
artifacts.content:
Subject: I stayed

At six each morning, Mara dusted the station piano. Its lowest key stayed down. She cleaned around it because the repair notice had been there longer than she had.

On a wet Thursday, she found a folded score beneath the lid. Every bar held the same small chord. Above it, someone had written: Play this when you can stay until it stops.

Mara had seven minutes before the next platform needed cleaning. She played the chord once. A man beside the departures board lowered his phone. A child stopped dragging her suitcase.

The broken key held one note after Mara lifted her hands. She waited with the others. When the note finally faded, her seven minutes were gone. She folded the score and left it where she had found it.

The next morning, the score was still there. Beneath the instruction, another hand had added: I stayed.

A writing exercise

Choose an ordinary object that has a small fault: a piano key, a torn pocket, a clock that loses a minute. Give someone a practical reason to handle it.

Write a scene in which the fault makes that person wait. Let somebody else notice. Finish with two words left behind.

You can borrow the exercise and choose your own setting. Keep Mara's story as a reading example. If you turn your scene into audio, use your own music or a score you have permission to use.

Reply with your two final words if you would like to share them.

artifacts.title: The station piano: narration script
artifacts.content:
Narration draft, approximately 45-60 seconds after rehearsal. No recording has been made.

At six each morning, Mara dusted the station piano.
Its lowest key stayed down.

On a wet Thursday, she found a score beneath the lid.
One chord, repeated.
Above it: Play this when you can stay until it stops.

She had seven minutes.
She played once.

A man lowered his phone.
A child stopped dragging her suitcase.

The broken key held a note after Mara lifted her hands.
They waited.

When the sound faded, her seven minutes were gone.

The next morning, someone had written beneath the instruction:
I stayed.

Shot direction: piano key, folded paper, hands, suitcase wheel, the final handwritten words. Hold the last frame long enough to read it. Record original narration; choose original or licensed music.
